newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BRAZIL FINALLY GIVE CHANCE TO ANDERSON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL FINALLY GIVE CHANCE TO ANDERSON.

text.p: Brazil's French-based striker Anderson, consistently overlooked by his country, was finally rewarded with a national team call-up Tuesday.

The Monaco player, who has enjoyed years of success in French football, was one of three uncapped players included the squad for next month's brief Far East tour. His absence from the team has been one of the great injustices and mysteries of Brazilian soccer.
Flamengo defender Junior Baiano and Sao Paulo striker Dodo were the other uncapped players.
Dodo's inclusion had been widely expected. He began this season as a reserve with his club but quickly made his mark and finished as top scorer in the Sao Paulo championship with 19 goals.
Last week he scored all his side's goals in the 5-0 win away to Cruzeiro in the Brazilian championship.

Coach Mario Zagallo left striker Romario out of the squad and dropped midfielders Djalminha and defender Celio Silva, who joined English champions Manchester United last week. Both played in the Copa America last month.
Atletico Madrid midfielder Juninho, left out of the Copa America team, was recalled while Deportivo Coruna's Rivaldo was brought back for the first time since the Atlanta Olympics.
Fourteen members of the victorious Copa America squad were included.
Brazil are away to South Korea and Japan on the tour.
Goalkeepers - Taffarel (Atletico Mineiro), Carlos Germano (Vasco da Gama)
Defenders - Ze Maria (Parma) Junior Baiano (Flamengo), Goncalves (Botafogo), Cafu, Aldair (Roma), Andre Cruz (Napoli), Roberto Carlos (Real Madrid)

Midfielders - Dunga (Jubilo Iwata), Cesar Sampaio (Yokohama Flugels), Denilson (Sao Paulo), Ricardinho (Cruzeiro), Juninho (Atletico Madrid), Flavio Conceicao, Rivaldo (Deportivo Coruna),Leonardo (Paris St.Germain), Ze Roberto (Real Madrid)
Forwards - Ronaldo (Barcelona/Internazionale), Donizete Corinthians), Dodo (Sao Paulo), Anderson (Monaco)
